traits.leaf_width_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Koeleria cristata: blades 1 mm to 3 mm wide.

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Koeleria cristata: culms 30 cm to 60 cm tall.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Koeleria cristata: panicle 4 cm to 15 cm long.

appearance.organs.panicle.note: The panicle's layout, the model's choice after FNA (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page was not read): dense and spike-like, interrupted at the base. Drawn as 30 short branches in threes close to the axis, each with about 8 spikelets. FNA's lemmas run as long as its spikelets, which would stack the two florets at one height, so each lemma is drawn 0.75 of the florets' height. Colours by eye: silvery green.

traits.note: FNA's account of the species (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): panicles 4 to 27 cm long and 0.5 to 2 cm wide, interrupted at the base, otherwise dense; spikelets 2.5 to 6.5 mm, with 2(3) florets; glumes 2.5 to 5 mm; lemmas 2.5 to 6.5 mm, shiny. Whether the lemma's midvein ends in an awn of about 1 mm (FNA) or only a point (GrassBase: 0 to 0.4 mm) is left open, so no awn is stated.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, tufted bunchgrass with short blades and dense, spike-like, shining silvery panicles. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.4 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: grey-green blades; silvery panicles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.life_span.note: Hitchcock (p. 276, K. cristata, the name he used for this plant): a tufted perennial.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Hitchcock (p. 276, K. cristata): a tufted perennial, no rhizomes named.

traits.clonal.note: Hitchcock (p. 276, K. cristata): tufted, with no rhizomes or stolons named; he adds that the plants are rather scattered.

traits.lower_glume_length_m.note: Hitchcock (p. 276-277, K. cristata): glumes and lemmas scaberulous, 3 to 4 mm long; the genus has the lower glume narrow and sometimes shorter than the upper.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Hitchcock (p. 276, K. cristata): panicle erect, spikelike and dense (loose at flowering), tapering at the top.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): leaf-blades filiform or linear, 5-20 cm long, 1-2.5 mm wide.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 1 (Koeleria no. 2, K. cristata, fig. 385): flowers June-July on prairies.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS's prairie Junegrass review (Simonin 2000, read 2026-10-16): in southern Idaho "seed ripening occurring mid-July" and dissemination from mid-July to mid-August (it also says seed "ripens late summer to fall" in general); read as July and August.
